title: Integration test: SSH host-key verification against local sshd

Defer to dedicated bead so 9es stays offline-runnable.

title: Wire /healthz and /readyz HTTP endpoints
description: Synchrotron-server currently exposes only /metrics on its HTTP listener. The Helm chart (58v.2) ships TCP probes as a workaround. Add proper /healthz (always 200 once axum is up) and /readyz (200 once DB open and config loaded) endpoints, then switch the chart's default probes back to httpGet.
close_reason: ReadinessGate (Arc<AtomicBool>) + probes_router(gate) exposing /healthz (always 200 once axum routes), /livez (alias), /readyz (200 when gate flipped, 503 otherwise). main.rs marks ready after DB+listener init. Helm chart probes flipped back to httpGet on /healthz and /readyz. 4 unit tests.

title: End-to-end Smart Diff pipeline + kind cluster test
description: Wire the four xje tiers (SSA dry-run → auto-ignore → user ignore → ownership filter) into a single SmartDiffPipeline used by the reconciler, and prove it on a kind cluster: HPA-targeted Deployment plus a mutating webhook should produce no false positive on spec.replicas while still surfacing genuine image drift. Closes the second acceptance criterion of synchrotron-cd-xje.
close_reason: SmartDiffPipeline at synchrotron-diff::pipeline composes the four xje tiers: applier.normalize → compare::diff → auto_ignore_rules_for(target, &cache).apply → user_rules.apply → FieldOwnershipFilter::apply. Generic over DryRunApplier (mock for unit tests, KubeDryRunApplier for production). 7 unit tests + env-gated kind integration test at crates/synchrotron-kube/tests/kind_smart_diff.rs proving the second xje acceptance criterion: HPA-targeted Deployment with autoscaler-bumped replicas (patched as kube-controller-manager to mirror real ownership) produces zero drift on spec.replicas (auto-ignore swallows), while bumping the container image surfaces image drift cleanly.

title: Cluster discovery + informer wiring for ScalerCache
description: Wire kube-rs list/watch informers for HPA, VPA, and KEDA ScaledObject in synchrotron-kube. On add/update/delete, parse via synchrotron_diff::parse_scaler and update a shared ScalerCache atomically. Periodic full refresh every 5 min as backstop. Pure-Rust core (parse_scaler + ScalerCache) already shipped in xje.2.
close_reason: ScalerDiscovery in synchrotron-kube::scaler_discovery wires three Informer<DynamicObject> (HPA, VPA, KEDA ScaledObject) into a shared Arc<RwLock<ScalerCache>>. Source-indexed map per-controller-partition; Applied/Deleted update incrementally, Restarted replaces only its own partition. kube-rs watcher's relist on watch errors gives the periodic-refresh backstop without a separate timer racing it. spawn_for_cluster() helper resolves ApiResources via discovery and silently skips kinds the cluster doesn't have (common for VPA/KEDA). Added Hash to ControllerKind. 5 unit tests using scripted WatchFactory streams: all-three-kinds populate, VPA off-mode filtered, applied-then-deleted clears, partition-isolation under restart, drop cleans up tasks.

title: Kind-cluster integration test for KubeDryRunApplier

Env-gated (SYNCHROTRON_KIND_TEST=1) so it stays off the default test path. Closes the deferred xje.1 acceptance criterion.
close_reason: Env-gated kind-cluster integration test (SYNCHROTRON_KIND_TEST=1) at crates/synchrotron-kube/tests/kind_dry_run.rs. Asserts dry-run round-trip (1) carries server-defaulted fields proving the request traversed the mutating-admission pipeline (terminationGracePeriodSeconds, imagePullPolicy), and (2) dry-run .spec equals the .spec of a real (non-dry) SSA against the same cluster — the strongest claim from the acceptance criterion. External-webhook variant (e.g., Kyverno-installed mutation policy) can be added later as additive coverage; built-in admission defaulting already exercises the same wire path.

title: Periodic auto-heal scheduler

close_reason: Landed periodic auto-heal scheduler. AutoHealConfig (default interval 180s, jitter_fraction 0.1) + AppLister trait. AutoHealScheduler::spawn runs a task that sleeps(interval) then ticks — per tick, iterates apps and enqueue_coalesce(AutoHeal) each with per-app delay = interval*jitter_fraction/N for deterministic uniform spread (no RNG needed, load-spreading is the goal). Skip-while-in-flight is automatic via enqueue_coalesce; a dedicated 'skipped' counter tracks how much auto-heal work was redundant with event-driven reconciles. AutoHealStats exposes ticks/enqueued/skipped. 5 tests: first tick fires after interval with AutoHeal tag, in-flight apps skipped + counted, empty app list still ticks, jitter spacing observable in enqueue timestamps, ticks counter increments over time. Total 33 tests in crate.

Coalescing via PoolHandle::enqueue_coalesce (skip if app already pending/in-flight, since the next reconcile will observe the latest desired state anyway). 5 integration tests: repo-change fans out to mapped apps, webhook tags trigger correctly, rapid bursts coalesce to single enqueue, unrelated events no-op, unknown repos no-op. Total 28 tests in crate.

title: Per-app reconcile function
description: For a single app: fetch desired manifests from cache, fetch live state from informer cache, run smart diff, decide sync/noop, record outcome. Idempotent and safe to re-run.

- Handles missing app / missing cluster gracefully
- Unit tests covering drift, no-drift, partial failures
close_reason: Landed pure planner + reconcile wrapper. plan.rs: pure plan(desired, live) -> Plan returning sorted PlanEntry list with PlannedAction::{Apply, Delete, NoOp}, identity by (Gvk, namespace, name), YAML-body equality for drift check (smarter diff stripping server-side fields is a later slice). reconcile.rs: Reconciler with DesiredSource/LiveSource traits (sync, backed by AppCache + informer cache in prod), reconcile_app(app, cluster) fetches both, calls plan, always publishes SystemEvent::SyncOutcome (success or failure message). title: Bounded HTTP/2 pool sizing per cluster
description: Wire max_idle_per_host (and related hyper pool knobs) through ClusterConfig into the kube client. Currently KubeClient uses kube-rs defaults via Client::try_from(config). To bound the pool we need to construct a hyper_util Client with builder().pool_max_idle_per_host(n), layer kube::client::ConfigExt service layers on it, then Client::new(service, ns). Deferred from h48.8.1 because it's additive to working code and not on the critical path for downstream sub-issues.
notes: Investigated kube-rs 0.95: Config has no pool_max_idle_per_host knob. Wiring this requires replicating make_generic_builder (kube-client 0.95 src/client/builder.rs:121–230) — building hyper_util::client::legacy::Builder ourselves with the pool setting, then re-stacking base_uri_layer, auth_layer, extra_headers_layer, gzip DecompressionLayer, TraceLayer, TimeoutConnector, and the rustls/openssl feature-gated TLS selection. Risk: silent drift if kube-rs adds new default layers. Recommendation: wait for upstream to expose a builder hook (track kube-rs issue tracker), or revisit if HTTP/2 multiplexing causes prod incidents. Deferred from active work — h48.8 epic considered functionally complete without it.
